threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to complain about the weather in late April—it’s just a rite of passage here.
Caught a guy in a full penguin suit on the 196 last Saturday. He was practicing his waddle, claiming it was for a charity event. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw my neighbor negotiating a peace treaty between two street cats over a patch of sun—this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you sip coffee while watching spontaneous techno parties erupt in the streets, complete with glow sticks and eccentric dance moves.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they instinctively step over the coffee spill on the sidewalk instead of avoiding it. It’s just part of the scene.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Nothing like a dog on the tracks at Civic Center to slow everyone down—just another day in SF where even the pups have to make their mark.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plaça, but the real charm is in the little streets where locals barter for fresh produce. It's a different world.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their hesitation at the menu—struggling with the Catalan names while the locals are already ordering with ease.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check for a signal on your phone while waiting for the Overground; local veterans know the dead zones by heart.
Caught a chap on the 59 last night singing opera to his reflection in the window. Only in Brixton, eh? The night bus brings out the hidden talents.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid selling homemade lemonade outside a Späti while a group of hipsters argued about vinyl records was when I felt at home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a 'silent disco' party in an old warehouse, where everyone dances to their own music, but together.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they casually navigate the pigeons near 24th and Mission, while newcomers flinch and dodge.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 this morning—driver handed a sandwich to a guy who looked like he needed it more than we did. Muni’s not just transit; it’s humanity on wheels.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the best tapas are in La Rambla, but the hidden gems are in the backstreets of Gràcia where locals gather.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at how the baker gives you two different types of bread for one price—completely unprepared for such generosity.
